Service: EC2 | Action: CreateTags | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 createtags --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Adds or overwrites only the specified tags for the specified Amazon EC2 resource or resources. When you specify an existing tag key, the value is overwritten with the new value. Each resource can have a maximum of 50 tags. Each tag consists of a key and optional value. Tag keys must be unique per resource.

For more information about tags, see Tag your Amazon EC2 resources in the Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud User Guide. For more information about creating IAM policies that control users' access to resources based on tags, see Supported resource-level permissions for Amazon EC2 API actions in the Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud User Guide.

Service: EC2 | Action: CreateTrafficMirrorFilter | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 createtrafficmirrorfilter --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Creates a Traffic Mirror filter.

A Traffic Mirror filter is a set of rules that defines the traffic to mirror.

By default, no traffic is mirrored. To mirror traffic, use CreateTrafficMirrorFilterRule to add Traffic Mirror rules to the filter. The rules you add define what traffic gets mirrored. You can also use ModifyTrafficMirrorFilterNetworkServices to mirror supported network services.

Service: EC2 | Action: CreateTrafficMirrorFilterRule | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 createtrafficmirrorfilterrule --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Creates a Traffic Mirror filter rule.

A Traffic Mirror rule defines the Traffic Mirror source traffic to mirror.

You need the Traffic Mirror filter ID when you create the rule.

Service: EC2 | Action: CreateTrafficMirrorSession | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 createtrafficmirrorsession --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Creates a Traffic Mirror session.

A Traffic Mirror session actively copies packets from a Traffic Mirror source to a Traffic Mirror target. Create a filter, and then assign it to the session to define a subset of the traffic to mirror, for example all TCP traffic.

The Traffic Mirror source and the Traffic Mirror target (monitoring appliances) can be in the same VPC, or in a different VPC connected via VPC peering or a transit gateway.

By default, no traffic is mirrored. Use CreateTrafficMirrorFilter to create filter rules that specify the traffic to mirror.

Service: EC2 | Action: CreateTrafficMirrorTarget | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 createtrafficmirrortarget --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Creates a target for your Traffic Mirror session.

A Traffic Mirror target is the destination for mirrored traffic. The Traffic Mirror source and the Traffic Mirror target (monitoring appliances) can be in the same VPC, or in different VPCs connected via VPC peering or a transit gateway.

A Traffic Mirror target can be a network interface, a Network Load Balancer, or a Gateway Load Balancer endpoint.

To use the target in a Traffic Mirror session, use CreateTrafficMirrorSession.

Service: EC2 | Action: CreateTransitGateway | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 createtransitgateway --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Creates a transit gateway.

You can use a transit gateway to interconnect your virtual private clouds (VPC) and on-premises networks. After the transit gateway enters the available state, you can attach your VPCs and VPN connections to the transit gateway.

To attach your VPCs, use CreateTransitGatewayVpcAttachment.

To attach a VPN connection, use CreateCustomerGateway to create a customer gateway and specify the ID of the customer gateway and the ID of the transit gateway in a call to CreateVpnConnection.

When you create a transit gateway, we create a default transit gateway route table and use it as the default association route table and the default propagation route table. You can use CreateTransitGatewayRouteTable to create additional transit gateway route tables. If you disable automatic route propagation, we do not create a default transit gateway route table. You can use EnableTransitGatewayRouteTablePropagation to propagate routes from a resource attachment to a transit gateway route table. If you disable automatic associations, you can use AssociateTransitGatewayRouteTable to associate a resource attachment with a transit gateway route table.

Service: EC2 | Action: CreateTransitGatewayConnect | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 createtransitgatewayconnect --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Creates a Connect attachment from a specified transit gateway attachment. A Connect attachment is a GRE-based tunnel attachment that you can use to establish a connection between a transit gateway and an appliance.

A Connect attachment uses an existing VPC or Amazon Web Services Direct Connect attachment as the underlying transport mechanism.

Service: EC2 | Action: CreateTransitGatewayConnectPeer | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 createtransitgatewayconnectpeer --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Creates a Connect peer for a specified transit gateway Connect attachment between a transit gateway and an appliance.

The peer address and transit gateway address must be the same IP address family (IPv4 or IPv6).

For more information, see Connect peers in the Amazon Web Services Transit Gateways Guide.

Service: EC2 | Action: CreateTransitGatewayMeteringPolicy | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 createtransitgatewaymeteringpolicy --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Creates a metering policy for a transit gateway to track and measure network traffic.

Service: EC2 | Action: CreateTransitGatewayMeteringPolicyEntry | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 createtransitgatewaymeteringpolicyentry --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Creates an entry in a transit gateway metering policy to define traffic measurement rules.

Service: EC2 | Action: CreateTransitGatewayMulticastDomain | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 createtransitgatewaymulticastdomain --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Creates a multicast domain using the specified transit gateway.

The transit gateway must be in the available state before you create a domain. Use DescribeTransitGateways to see the state of transit gateway.

Service: EC2 | Action: CreateTransitGatewayPeeringAttachment | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 createtransitgatewaypeeringattachment --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Requests a transit gateway peering attachment between the specified transit gateway (requester) and a peer transit gateway (accepter). The peer transit gateway can be in your account or a different Amazon Web Services account.

After you create the peering attachment, the owner of the accepter transit gateway must accept the attachment request.

Service: EC2 | Action: CreateTransitGatewayPolicyTable | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 createtransitgatewaypolicytable --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Creates a transit gateway policy table.

Service: EC2 | Action: CreateTransitGatewayPrefixListReference | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 createtransitgatewayprefixlistreference --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Creates a reference (route) to a prefix list in a specified transit gateway route table.

Service: EC2 | Action: CreateTransitGatewayRoute | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 createtransitgatewayroute --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Creates a static route for the specified transit gateway route table.

Service: EC2 | Action: CreateTransitGatewayRouteTable | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 createtransitgatewayroutetable --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Creates a route table for the specified transit gateway.

Service: EC2 | Action: CreateTransitGatewayRouteTableAnnouncement | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 createtransitgatewayroutetableannouncement --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Advertises a new transit gateway route table.

Service: EC2 | Action: CreateTransitGatewayVpcAttachment | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 createtransitgatewayvpcattachment --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Attaches the specified VPC to the specified transit gateway.

If you attach a VPC with a CIDR range that overlaps the CIDR range of a VPC that is already attached, the new VPC CIDR range is not propagated to the default propagation route table.

To send VPC traffic to an attached transit gateway, add a route to the VPC route table using CreateRoute.

Service: EC2 | Action: CreateVerifiedAccessEndpoint | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 createverifiedaccessendpoint --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

An Amazon Web Services Verified Access endpoint is where you define your application along with an optional endpoint-level access policy.

Service: EC2 | Action: CreateVerifiedAccessGroup | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 createverifiedaccessgroup --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

An Amazon Web Services Verified Access group is a collection of Amazon Web Services Verified Access endpoints who's associated applications have similar security requirements. Each instance within a Verified Access group shares an Verified Access policy. For example, you can group all Verified Access instances associated with "sales" applications together and use one common Verified Access policy.

Service: EC2 | Action: CreateVerifiedAccessInstance | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 createverifiedaccessinstance --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

An Amazon Web Services Verified Access instance is a regional entity that evaluates application requests and grants access only when your security requirements are met.

Service: EC2 | Action: CreateVerifiedAccessTrustProvider | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 createverifiedaccesstrustprovider --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

A trust provider is a third-party entity that creates, maintains, and manages identity information for users and devices. When an application request is made, the identity information sent by the trust provider is evaluated by Verified Access before allowing or denying the application request.

Service: EC2 | Action: CreateVolume | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 createvolume --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Creates an EBS volume that can be attached to an instance in the same Availability Zone.

You can create a new empty volume or restore a volume from an EBS snapshot. Any Amazon Web Services Marketplace product codes from the snapshot are propagated to the volume.

You can create encrypted volumes. Encrypted volumes must be attached to instances that support Amazon EBS encryption. Volumes that are created from encrypted snapshots are also automatically encrypted. For more information, see Amazon EBS encryption in the Amazon EBS User Guide.

You can tag your volumes during creation. For more information, see Tag your Amazon EC2 resources in the Amazon EC2 User Guide.

For more information, see Create an Amazon EBS volume in the Amazon EBS User Guide.

Service: EC2 | Action: CreateVpc | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 createvpc --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Creates a VPC with the specified CIDR blocks.

A VPC must have an associated IPv4 CIDR block. You can choose an IPv4 CIDR block or an IPAM-allocated IPv4 CIDR block. You can optionally associate an IPv6 CIDR block with a VPC. You can choose an IPv6 CIDR block, an Amazon-provided IPv6 CIDR block, an IPAM-allocated IPv6 CIDR block, or an IPv6 CIDR block that you brought to Amazon Web Services. For more information, see IP addressing for your VPCs and subnets in the Amazon VPC User Guide.

By default, each instance that you launch in the VPC has the default DHCP options, which include only a default DNS server that we provide (AmazonProvidedDNS). For more information, see DHCP option sets in the Amazon VPC User Guide.

You can specify DNS options and tenancy for a VPC when you create it. You can't change the tenancy of a VPC after you create it. For more information, see VPC configuration options in the Amazon VPC User Guide.

Service: EC2 | Action: CreateVpcBlockPublicAccessExclusion | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 createvpcblockpublicaccessexclusion --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Create a VPC Block Public Access (BPA) exclusion. A VPC BPA exclusion is a mode that can be applied to a single VPC or subnet that exempts it from the account’s BPA mode and will allow bidirectional or egress-only access. You can create BPA exclusions for VPCs and subnets even when BPA is not enabled on the account to ensure that there is no traffic disruption to the exclusions when VPC BPA is turned on. To learn more about VPC BPA, see Block public access to VPCs and subnets in the Amazon VPC User Guide.

Service: EC2 | Action: CreateVpcEncryptionControl | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 createvpcencryptioncontrol --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Creates a VPC Encryption Control configuration for a specified VPC. VPC Encryption Control enables you to enforce encryption for all data in transit within and between VPCs to meet compliance requirements for standards like HIPAA, FedRAMP, and PCI DSS.

For more information, see Enforce VPC encryption in transit in the Amazon VPC User Guide.

Service: EC2 | Action: CreateVpcEndpoint | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 createvpcendpoint --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Creates a VPC endpoint. A VPC endpoint provides a private connection between the specified VPC and the specified endpoint service. You can use an endpoint service provided by Amazon Web Services, an Amazon Web Services Marketplace Partner, or another Amazon Web Services account. For more information, see the Amazon Web Services PrivateLink User Guide.

Service: EC2 | Action: CreateVpcEndpointConnectionNotification | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 createvpcendpointconnectionnotification --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Creates a connection notification for a specified VPC endpoint or VPC endpoint service. A connection notification notifies you of specific endpoint events. You must create an SNS topic to receive notifications. For more information, see Creating an Amazon SNS topic in the Amazon SNS Developer Guide.

You can create a connection notification for interface endpoints only.

Service: EC2 | Action: CreateVpcEndpointServiceConfiguration | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 createvpcendpointserviceconfiguration --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Creates a VPC endpoint service to which service consumers (Amazon Web Services accounts, users, and IAM roles) can connect.

Before you create an endpoint service, you must create one of the following for your service:

  • A Network Load Balancer. Service consumers connect to your service using an interface endpoint.

  • A Gateway Load Balancer. Service consumers connect to your service using a Gateway Load Balancer endpoint.

If you set the private DNS name, you must prove that you own the private DNS domain name.

For more information, see the Amazon Web Services PrivateLink Guide.

Service: EC2 | Action: CreateVpcPeeringConnection | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 createvpcpeeringconnection --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Requests a VPC peering connection between two VPCs: a requester VPC that you own and an accepter VPC with which to create the connection. The accepter VPC can belong to another Amazon Web Services account and can be in a different Region to the requester VPC. The requester VPC and accepter VPC cannot have overlapping CIDR blocks.

Limitations and rules apply to a VPC peering connection. For more information, see the VPC peering limitations in the VPC Peering Guide.

The owner of the accepter VPC must accept the peering request to activate the peering connection. The VPC peering connection request expires after 7 days, after which it cannot be accepted or rejected.

If you create a VPC peering connection request between VPCs with overlapping CIDR blocks, the VPC peering connection has a status of failed.

Service: EC2 | Action: CreateVpnConcentrator | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 createvpnconcentrator --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Creates a VPN concentrator that aggregates multiple VPN connections to a transit gateway.

Service: EC2 | Action: CreateVpnConnection | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 createvpnconnection --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Creates a VPN connection between an existing virtual private gateway or transit gateway and a customer gateway. The supported connection type is ipsec.1.

The response includes information that you need to give to your network administrator to configure your customer gateway.

We strongly recommend that you use HTTPS when calling this operation because the response contains sensitive cryptographic information for configuring your customer gateway device.

If you decide to shut down your VPN connection for any reason and later create a new VPN connection, you must reconfigure your customer gateway with the new information returned from this call.

This is an idempotent operation. If you perform the operation more than once, Amazon EC2 doesn't return an error.

For more information, see Amazon Web Services Site-to-Site VPN in the Amazon Web Services Site-to-Site VPN User Guide.

Service: EC2 | Action: CreateVpnConnectionRoute | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 createvpnconnectionroute --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Creates a static route associated with a VPN connection between an existing virtual private gateway and a VPN customer gateway. The static route allows traffic to be routed from the virtual private gateway to the VPN customer gateway.

For more information, see Amazon Web Services Site-to-Site VPN in the Amazon Web Services Site-to-Site VPN User Guide.

Service: EC2 | Action: CreateVpnGateway | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 createvpngateway --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Creates a virtual private gateway. A virtual private gateway is the endpoint on the VPC side of your VPN connection. You can create a virtual private gateway before creating the VPC itself.

For more information, see Amazon Web Services Site-to-Site VPN in the Amazon Web Services Site-to-Site VPN User Guide.

Service: EC2 | Action: DeleteCapacityManagerDataExport | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 deletecapacitymanagerdataexport --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Deletes an existing Capacity Manager data export configuration. This stops future scheduled exports but does not delete previously exported files from S3.

Service: EC2 | Action: DeleteCarrierGateway | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 deletecarriergateway --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Deletes a carrier gateway.

If you do not delete the route that contains the carrier gateway as the Target, the route is a blackhole route. For information about how to delete a route, see DeleteRoute.

Service: EC2 | Action: DeleteClientVpnEndpoint | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 deleteclientvpnendpoint --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Deletes the specified Client VPN endpoint. You must disassociate all target networks before you can delete a Client VPN endpoint.

Service: EC2 | Action: DeleteClientVpnRoute | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 deleteclientvpnroute --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Deletes a route from a Client VPN endpoint. You can only delete routes that you manually added using the CreateClientVpnRoute action. You cannot delete routes that were automatically added when associating a subnet. To remove routes that have been automatically added, disassociate the target subnet from the Client VPN endpoint.

Service: EC2 | Action: DeleteCoipCidr | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 deletecoipcidr --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Deletes a range of customer-owned IP addresses.

Service: EC2 | Action: DeleteCoipPool | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 deletecoippool --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Deletes a pool of customer-owned IP (CoIP) addresses.

Service: EC2 | Action: DeleteCustomerGateway | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 deletecustomergateway --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Deletes the specified customer gateway. You must delete the VPN connection before you can delete the customer gateway.

Service: EC2 | Action: DeleteDhcpOptions | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 deletedhcpoptions --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Deletes the specified set of DHCP options. You must disassociate the set of DHCP options before you can delete it. You can disassociate the set of DHCP options by associating either a new set of options or the default set of options with the VPC.

Service: EC2 | Action: DeleteEgressOnlyInternetGateway | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 deleteegressonlyinternetgateway --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Deletes an egress-only internet gateway.

Service: EC2 | Action: DeleteFleets | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 deletefleets --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Deletes the specified EC2 Fleet request.

After you delete an EC2 Fleet request, it launches no new instances.

You must also specify whether a deleted EC2 Fleet request should terminate its instances. If you choose to terminate the instances, the EC2 Fleet request enters the deleted_terminating state. Otherwise, it enters the deleted_running state, and the instances continue to run until they are interrupted or you terminate them manually.

A deleted instant fleet with running instances is not supported. When you delete an instant fleet, Amazon EC2 automatically terminates all its instances. For fleets with more than 1000 instances, the deletion request might fail. If your fleet has more than 1000 instances, first terminate most of the instances manually, leaving 1000 or fewer. Then delete the fleet, and the remaining instances will be terminated automatically.

Terminating an instance is permanent and irreversible.

After you terminate an instance, you can no longer connect to it, and it can't be recovered. All attached Amazon EBS volumes that are configured to be deleted on termination are also permanently deleted and can't be recovered. All data stored on instance store volumes is permanently lost. For more information, see How instance termination works.

Before you terminate an instance, ensure that you have backed up all data that you need to retain after the termination to persistent storage.

Restrictions

  • You can delete up to 25 fleets of type instant in a single request.

  • You can delete up to 100 fleets of type maintain or request in a single request.

  • You can delete up to 125 fleets in a single request, provided you do not exceed the quota for each fleet type, as specified above.

  • If you exceed the specified number of fleets to delete, no fleets are deleted.

For more information, see Delete an EC2 Fleet request and the instances in the fleet in the Amazon EC2 User Guide.

Service: EC2 | Action: DeleteFlowLogs | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 deleteflowlogs --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Deletes one or more flow logs.

Service: EC2 | Action: DeleteFpgaImage | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 deletefpgaimage --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Deletes the specified Amazon FPGA Image (AFI).

Service: EC2 | Action: DeleteImageUsageReport | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 deleteimageusagereport --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Deletes the specified image usage report.

For more information, see View your AMI usage in the Amazon EC2 User Guide.

Service: EC2 | Action: DeleteInstanceConnectEndpoint | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 deleteinstanceconnectendpoint --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Deletes the specified EC2 Instance Connect Endpoint.

Service: EC2 | Action: DeleteInstanceEventWindow | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 deleteinstanceeventwindow --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Deletes the specified event window.

For more information, see Define event windows for scheduled events in the Amazon EC2 User Guide.

Service: EC2 | Action: DeleteInternetGateway | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 deleteinternetgateway --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Deletes the specified internet gateway. You must detach the internet gateway from the VPC before you can delete it.

Service: EC2 | Action: DeleteIpam | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 deleteipam --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Delete an IPAM. Deleting an IPAM removes all monitored data associated with the IPAM including the historical data for CIDRs.

For more information, see Delete an IPAM in the Amazon VPC IPAM User Guide.

Service: EC2 | Action: DeleteIpamExternalResourceVerificationToken | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 deleteipamexternalresourceverificationtoken --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Delete a verification token.

A verification token is an Amazon Web Services-generated random value that you can use to prove ownership of an external resource. For example, you can use a verification token to validate that you control a public IP address range when you bring an IP address range to Amazon Web Services (BYOIP).

Service: EC2 | Action: DeleteIpamPolicy | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 deleteipampolicy --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Deletes an IPAM policy.

An IPAM policy is a set of rules that define how public IPv4 addresses from IPAM pools are allocated to Amazon Web Services resources. Each rule maps an Amazon Web Services service to IPAM pools that the service will use to get IP addresses. A single policy can have multiple rules and be applied to multiple Amazon Web Services Regions. If the IPAM pool run out of addresses then the services fallback to Amazon-provided IP addresses. A policy can be applied to an individual Amazon Web Services account or an entity within Amazon Web Services Organizations.

Service: EC2 | Action: DeleteIpamPool | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 deleteipampool --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Delete an IPAM pool.

You cannot delete an IPAM pool if there are allocations in it or CIDRs provisioned to it. To release allocations, see ReleaseIpamPoolAllocation. To deprovision pool CIDRs, see DeprovisionIpamPoolCidr.

For more information, see Delete a pool in the Amazon VPC IPAM User Guide.

Service: EC2 | Action: DeleteIpamPrefixListResolver | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 deleteipamprefixlistresolver --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Deletes an IPAM prefix list resolver. Before deleting a resolver, you must first delete all resolver targets associated with it.

Service: EC2 | Action: DeleteIpamPrefixListResolverTarget | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 deleteipamprefixlistresolvertarget --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Deletes an IPAM prefix list resolver target. This removes the association between the resolver and the managed prefix list, stopping automatic CIDR synchronization.

For more information about IPAM prefix list resolver, see Automate prefix list updates with IPAM in the Amazon VPC IPAM User Guide.

Service: EC2 | Action: DeleteIpamResourceDiscovery | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 deleteipamresourcediscovery --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Deletes an IPAM resource discovery. A resource discovery is an IPAM component that enables IPAM to manage and monitor resources that belong to the owning account.

Service: EC2 | Action: DeleteIpamScope | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 deleteipamscope --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Delete the scope for an IPAM. You cannot delete the default scopes.

For more information, see Delete a scope in the Amazon VPC IPAM User Guide.

Service: EC2 | Action: DeleteKeyPair | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 deletekeypair --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Deletes the specified key pair, by removing the public key from Amazon EC2.

Service: EC2 | Action: DeleteLaunchTemplate | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 deletelaunchtemplate --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Deletes a launch template. Deleting a launch template deletes all of its versions.

Service: EC2 | Action: DeleteLaunchTemplateVersions | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 deletelaunchtemplateversions --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Deletes one or more versions of a launch template.

You can't delete the default version of a launch template; you must first assign a different version as the default. If the default version is the only version for the launch template, you must delete the entire launch template using DeleteLaunchTemplate.

You can delete up to 200 launch template versions in a single request. To delete more than 200 versions in a single request, use DeleteLaunchTemplate, which deletes the launch template and all of its versions.

For more information, see Delete a launch template version in the Amazon EC2 User Guide.

Service: EC2 | Action: DeleteLocalGatewayRoute | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 deletelocalgatewayroute --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Deletes the specified route from the specified local gateway route table.

Service: EC2 | Action: DeleteLocalGatewayRouteTable | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 deletelocalgatewayroutetable --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Deletes a local gateway route table.

Service: EC2 | Action: DeleteLocalGatewayRouteTableVirtualInterfaceGroupAssociation | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 deletelocalgatewayroutetablevirtualinterfacegroupassociation --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Deletes a local gateway route table virtual interface group association.

Service: EC2 | Action: DeleteLocalGatewayRouteTableVpcAssociation | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 deletelocalgatewayroutetablevpcassociation --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Deletes the specified association between a VPC and local gateway route table.

Service: EC2 | Action: DeleteLocalGatewayVirtualInterface | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 deletelocalgatewayvirtualinterface --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Deletes the specified local gateway virtual interface.

Service: EC2 | Action: DeleteLocalGatewayVirtualInterfaceGroup | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 deletelocalgatewayvirtualinterfacegroup --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Delete the specified local gateway interface group.

Service: EC2 | Action: DeleteManagedPrefixList | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 deletemanagedprefixlist --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Deletes the specified managed prefix list. You must first remove all references to the prefix list in your resources.

Service: EC2 | Action: DeleteNatGateway | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 deletenatgateway --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Deletes the specified NAT gateway. Deleting a public NAT gateway disassociates its Elastic IP address, but does not release the address from your account. Deleting a NAT gateway does not delete any NAT gateway routes in your route tables.

Service: EC2 | Action: DeleteNetworkAcl | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 deletenetworkacl --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Deletes the specified network ACL. You can't delete the ACL if it's associated with any subnets. You can't delete the default network ACL.

Service: EC2 | Action: DeleteNetworkAclEntry | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 deletenetworkaclentry --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Deletes the specified ingress or egress entry (rule) from the specified network ACL.

Service: EC2 | Action: DeleteNetworkInsightsAccessScope | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 deletenetworkinsightsaccessscope --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Deletes the specified Network Access Scope.

Service: EC2 | Action: DeleteNetworkInsightsAccessScopeAnalysis | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 deletenetworkinsightsaccessscopeanalysis --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Deletes the specified Network Access Scope analysis.

Service: EC2 | Action: DeleteNetworkInsightsAnalysis | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 deletenetworkinsightsanalysis --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Deletes the specified network insights analysis.

Service: EC2 | Action: DeleteNetworkInsightsPath | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 deletenetworkinsightspath --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Deletes the specified path.

Service: EC2 | Action: DeleteNetworkInterface | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 deletenetworkinterface --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Deletes the specified network interface. You must detach the network interface before you can delete it.

Service: EC2 | Action: DeleteNetworkInterfacePermission | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 deletenetworkinterfacepermission --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Deletes a permission for a network interface. By default, you cannot delete the permission if the account for which you're removing the permission has attached the network interface to an instance. However, you can force delete the permission, regardless of any attachment.

Service: EC2 | Action: DeletePlacementGroup | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 deleteplacementgroup --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Deletes the specified placement group. You must terminate all instances in the placement group before you can delete the placement group. For more information, see Placement groups in the Amazon EC2 User Guide.

Service: EC2 | Action: DeletePublicIpv4Pool | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 deletepublicipv4pool --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Delete a public IPv4 pool. A public IPv4 pool is an EC2 IP address pool required for the public IPv4 CIDRs that you own and bring to Amazon Web Services to manage with IPAM. IPv6 addresses you bring to Amazon Web Services, however, use IPAM pools only.

Service: EC2 | Action: DeleteQueuedReservedInstances | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 deletequeuedreservedinstances --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Deletes the queued purchases for the specified Reserved Instances.

Service: EC2 | Action: DeleteRoute | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 deleteroute --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Deletes the specified route from the specified route table.

Service: EC2 | Action: DeleteRouteServer | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 deleterouteserver --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Deletes the specified route server.

Amazon VPC Route Server simplifies routing for traffic between workloads that are deployed within a VPC and its internet gateways. With this feature, VPC Route Server dynamically updates VPC and internet gateway route tables with your preferred IPv4 or IPv6 routes to achieve routing fault tolerance for those workloads. This enables you to automatically reroute traffic within a VPC, which increases the manageability of VPC routing and interoperability with third-party workloads.

Route server supports the follow route table types:

  • VPC route tables not associated with subnets

  • Subnet route tables

  • Internet gateway route tables

Route server does not support route tables associated with virtual private gateways. To propagate routes into a transit gateway route table, use Transit Gateway Connect.

For more information see Dynamic routing in your VPC with VPC Route Server in the Amazon VPC User Guide.

Service: EC2 | Action: DeleteRouteServerEndpoint | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 deleterouteserverendpoint --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Deletes the specified route server endpoint.

A route server endpoint is an Amazon Web Services-managed component inside a subnet that facilitates BGP (Border Gateway Protocol) connections between your route server and your BGP peers.

Service: EC2 | Action: DeleteRouteServerPeer | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 deleterouteserverpeer --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Deletes the specified BGP peer from a route server.

A route server peer is a session between a route server endpoint and the device deployed in Amazon Web Services (such as a firewall appliance or other network security function running on an EC2 instance). The device must meet these requirements:

  • Have an elastic network interface in the VPC

  • Support BGP (Border Gateway Protocol)

  • Can initiate BGP sessions

Service: EC2 | Action: DeleteRouteTable | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 deleteroutetable --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Deletes the specified route table. You must disassociate the route table from any subnets before you can delete it. You can't delete the main route table.

Service: EC2 | Action: DeleteSecondaryNetwork | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 deletesecondarynetwork --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Deletes a secondary network. You must delete all secondary subnets in the secondary network before you can delete the secondary network.

Service: EC2 | Action: DeleteSecondarySubnet | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 deletesecondarysubnet --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Deletes a secondary subnet. A secondary subnet must not contain any secondary interfaces prior to deletion.

Service: EC2 | Action: DeleteSecurityGroup | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 deletesecuritygroup --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Deletes a security group.

If you attempt to delete a security group that is associated with an instance or network interface, is referenced by another security group in the same VPC, or has a VPC association, the operation fails with DependencyViolation.

Service: EC2 | Action: DeleteSnapshot | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 deletesnapshot --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Deletes the specified snapshot.

When you make periodic snapshots of a volume, the snapshots are incremental, and only the blocks on the device that have changed since your last snapshot are saved in the new snapshot. When you delete a snapshot, only the data not needed for any other snapshot is removed. So regardless of which prior snapshots have been deleted, all active snapshots will have access to all the information needed to restore the volume.

You cannot delete a snapshot of the root device of an EBS volume used by a registered AMI. You must first deregister the AMI before you can delete the snapshot.

For more information, see Delete an Amazon EBS snapshot in the Amazon EBS User Guide.

Service: EC2 | Action: DeleteSpotDatafeedSubscription | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 deletespotdatafeedsubscription --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Deletes the data feed for Spot Instances.

Service: EC2 | Action: DeleteSubnet | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 deletesubnet --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Deletes the specified subnet. You must terminate all running instances in the subnet before you can delete the subnet.

Service: EC2 | Action: DeleteSubnetCidrReservation | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 deletesubnetcidrreservation --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Deletes a subnet CIDR reservation.

Service: EC2 | Action: DeleteTags | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 deletetags --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Deletes the specified set of tags from the specified set of resources.

To list the current tags, use DescribeTags. For more information about tags, see Tag your Amazon EC2 resources in the Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud User Guide.

Service: EC2 | Action: DeleteTrafficMirrorFilter | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 deletetrafficmirrorfilter --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Deletes the specified Traffic Mirror filter.

You cannot delete a Traffic Mirror filter that is in use by a Traffic Mirror session.

Service: EC2 | Action: DeleteTrafficMirrorFilterRule | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 deletetrafficmirrorfilterrule --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Deletes the specified Traffic Mirror rule.

Service: EC2 | Action: DeleteTrafficMirrorSession | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 deletetrafficmirrorsession --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Deletes the specified Traffic Mirror session.

Service: EC2 | Action: DeleteTrafficMirrorTarget | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 deletetrafficmirrortarget --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Deletes the specified Traffic Mirror target.

You cannot delete a Traffic Mirror target that is in use by a Traffic Mirror session.

Service: EC2 | Action: DeleteTransitGateway | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 deletetransitgateway --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Deletes the specified transit gateway.

Service: EC2 | Action: DeleteTransitGatewayConnect | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 deletetransitgatewayconnect --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Deletes the specified Connect attachment. You must first delete any Connect peers for the attachment.

Service: EC2 | Action: DeleteTransitGatewayConnectPeer | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 deletetransitgatewayconnectpeer --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Deletes the specified Connect peer.

Service: EC2 | Action: DeleteTransitGatewayMeteringPolicy | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 deletetransitgatewaymeteringpolicy --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Deletes a transit gateway metering policy.

Service: EC2 | Action: DeleteTransitGatewayMeteringPolicyEntry | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 deletetransitgatewaymeteringpolicyentry --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Deletes an entry from a transit gateway metering policy.

Service: EC2 | Action: DeleteTransitGatewayMulticastDomain | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 deletetransitgatewaymulticastdomain --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Deletes the specified transit gateway multicast domain.

Service: EC2 | Action: DeleteTransitGatewayPeeringAttachment | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 deletetransitgatewaypeeringattachment --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Deletes a transit gateway peering attachment.

Service: EC2 | Action: DeleteTransitGatewayPolicyTable | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 deletetransitgatewaypolicytable --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Deletes the specified transit gateway policy table.

Service: EC2 | Action: DeleteTransitGatewayPrefixListReference | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 deletetransitgatewayprefixlistreference --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Deletes a reference (route) to a prefix list in a specified transit gateway route table.

Service: EC2 | Action: DeleteTransitGatewayRoute | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 deletetransitgatewayroute --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Deletes the specified route from the specified transit gateway route table.

Service: EC2 | Action: DeleteTransitGatewayRouteTable | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 deletetransitgatewayroutetable --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Deletes the specified transit gateway route table. If there are any route tables associated with the transit gateway route table, you must first run DisassociateRouteTable before you can delete the transit gateway route table. This removes any route tables associated with the transit gateway route table.

Service: EC2 | Action: DeleteTransitGatewayRouteTableAnnouncement | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 deletetransitgatewayroutetableannouncement --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Advertises to the transit gateway that a transit gateway route table is deleted.

Service: EC2 | Action: DeleteTransitGatewayVpcAttachment | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 deletetransitgatewayvpcattachment --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Deletes the specified VPC attachment.

Service: EC2 | Action: DeleteVerifiedAccessEndpoint | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 deleteverifiedaccessendpoint --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Delete an Amazon Web Services Verified Access endpoint.

Service: EC2 | Action: DeleteVerifiedAccessGroup | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 deleteverifiedaccessgroup --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Delete an Amazon Web Services Verified Access group.

Service: EC2 | Action: DeleteVerifiedAccessInstance | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 deleteverifiedaccessinstance --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Delete an Amazon Web Services Verified Access instance.

Service: EC2 | Action: DeleteVerifiedAccessTrustProvider | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 deleteverifiedaccesstrustprovider --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Delete an Amazon Web Services Verified Access trust provider.

Service: EC2 | Action: DeleteVolume | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 deletevolume --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Deletes the specified EBS volume. The volume must be in the available state (not attached to an instance).

The volume can remain in the deleting state for several minutes.

For more information, see Delete an Amazon EBS volume in the Amazon EBS User Guide.

Service: EC2 | Action: DeleteVpc | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 deletevpc --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Deletes the specified VPC. You must detach or delete all gateways and resources that are associated with the VPC before you can delete it. For example, you must terminate all instances running in the VPC, delete all security groups associated with the VPC (except the default one), delete all route tables associated with the VPC (except the default one), and so on. When you delete the VPC, it deletes the default security group, network ACL, and route table for the VPC.

If you created a flow log for the VPC that you are deleting, note that flow logs for deleted VPCs are eventually automatically removed.

Service: EC2 | Action: DeleteVpcBlockPublicAccessExclusion | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 deletevpcblockpublicaccessexclusion --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Delete a VPC Block Public Access (BPA) exclusion. A VPC BPA exclusion is a mode that can be applied to a single VPC or subnet that exempts it from the account’s BPA mode and will allow bidirectional or egress-only access. You can create BPA exclusions for VPCs and subnets even when BPA is not enabled on the account to ensure that there is no traffic disruption to the exclusions when VPC BPA is turned on. To learn more about VPC BPA, see Block public access to VPCs and subnets in the Amazon VPC User Guide.

Service: EC2 | Action: DeleteVpcEncryptionControl | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 deletevpcencryptioncontrol --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Deletes a VPC Encryption Control configuration. This removes the encryption policy enforcement from the specified VPC.

For more information, see Enforce VPC encryption in transit in the Amazon VPC User Guide.

Service: EC2 | Action: DeleteVpcEndpointConnectionNotifications | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 deletevpcendpointconnectionnotifications --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Deletes the specified VPC endpoint connection notifications.

Service: EC2 | Action: DeleteVpcEndpointServiceConfigurations | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 deletevpcendpointserviceconfigurations --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Deletes the specified VPC endpoint service configurations. Before you can delete an endpoint service configuration, you must reject any Available or PendingAcceptance interface endpoint connections that are attached to the service.

Service: EC2 | Action: DeleteVpcEndpoints | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 deletevpcendpoints --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Deletes the specified VPC endpoints.

When you delete a gateway endpoint, we delete the endpoint routes in the route tables for the endpoint.

When you delete a Gateway Load Balancer endpoint, we delete its endpoint network interfaces. You can only delete Gateway Load Balancer endpoints when the routes that are associated with the endpoint are deleted.

When you delete an interface endpoint, we delete its endpoint network interfaces.

Service: EC2 | Action: DeleteVpcPeeringConnection | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 deletevpcpeeringconnection --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Deletes a VPC peering connection. Either the owner of the requester VPC or the owner of the accepter VPC can delete the VPC peering connection if it's in the active state. The owner of the requester VPC can delete a VPC peering connection in the pending-acceptance state. You cannot delete a VPC peering connection that's in the failed or rejected state.

Service: EC2 | Action: DeleteVpnConcentrator | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 deletevpnconcentrator --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Deletes the specified VPN concentrator.

Service: EC2 | Action: DeleteVpnConnection | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 deletevpnconnection --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Deletes the specified VPN connection.

If you're deleting the VPC and its associated components, we recommend that you detach the virtual private gateway from the VPC and delete the VPC before deleting the VPN connection. If you believe that the tunnel credentials for your VPN connection have been compromised, you can delete the VPN connection and create a new one that has new keys, without needing to delete the VPC or virtual private gateway. If you create a new VPN connection, you must reconfigure the customer gateway device using the new configuration information returned with the new VPN connection ID.

For certificate-based authentication, delete all Certificate Manager (ACM) private certificates used for the Amazon Web Services-side tunnel endpoints for the VPN connection before deleting the VPN connection.

Service: EC2 | Action: DeleteVpnConnectionRoute | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 deletevpnconnectionroute --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Deletes the specified static route associated with a VPN connection between an existing virtual private gateway and a VPN customer gateway. The static route allows traffic to be routed from the virtual private gateway to the VPN customer gateway.

Service: EC2 | Action: DeleteVpnGateway | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 deletevpngateway --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Deletes the specified virtual private gateway. You must first detach the virtual private gateway from the VPC. Note that you don't need to delete the virtual private gateway if you plan to delete and recreate the VPN connection between your VPC and your network.

Service: EC2 | Action: DeprovisionByoipCidr | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 deprovisionbyoipcidr --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Releases the specified address range that you provisioned for use with your Amazon Web Services resources through bring your own IP addresses (BYOIP) and deletes the corresponding address pool.

Before you can release an address range, you must stop advertising it and you must not have any IP addresses allocated from its address range.

Service: EC2 | Action: DeprovisionIpamByoasn | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 deprovisionipambyoasn --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Deprovisions your Autonomous System Number (ASN) from your Amazon Web Services account. This action can only be called after any BYOIP CIDR associations are removed from your Amazon Web Services account with DisassociateIpamByoasn. For more information, see Tutorial: Bring your ASN to IPAM in the Amazon VPC IPAM guide.

Service: EC2 | Action: DeprovisionIpamPoolCidr | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 deprovisionipampoolcidr --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Deprovision a CIDR provisioned from an IPAM pool. If you deprovision a CIDR from a pool that has a source pool, the CIDR is recycled back into the source pool. For more information, see Deprovision pool CIDRs in the Amazon VPC IPAM User Guide.

Service: EC2 | Action: DeprovisionPublicIpv4PoolCidr | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 deprovisionpublicipv4poolcidr --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Deprovision a CIDR from a public IPv4 pool.

Service: EC2 | Action: DeregisterImage | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 deregisterimage --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Deregisters the specified AMI. A deregistered AMI can't be used to launch new instances.

If a deregistered EBS-backed AMI matches a Recycle Bin retention rule, it moves to the Recycle Bin for the specified retention period. It can be restored before its retention period expires, after which it is permanently deleted. If the deregistered AMI doesn't match a retention rule, it is permanently deleted immediately. For more information, see Recover deleted Amazon EBS snapshots and EBS-backed AMIs with Recycle Bin in the Amazon EBS User Guide.

When deregistering an EBS-backed AMI, you can optionally delete its associated snapshots at the same time. However, if a snapshot is associated with multiple AMIs, it won't be deleted even if specified for deletion, although the AMI will still be deregistered.

Deregistering an AMI does not delete the following:

  • Instances already launched from the AMI. You'll continue to incur usage costs for the instances until you terminate them.

  • For EBS-backed AMIs: Snapshots that are associated with multiple AMIs. You'll continue to incur snapshot storage costs.

  • For instance store-backed AMIs: The files uploaded to Amazon S3 during AMI creation. You'll continue to incur S3 storage costs.

For more information, see Deregister an Amazon EC2 AMI in the Amazon EC2 User Guide.

Service: EC2 | Action: DeregisterInstanceEventNotificationAttributes | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 deregisterinstanceeventnotificationattributes --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Deregisters tag keys to prevent tags that have the specified tag keys from being included in scheduled event notifications for resources in the Region.

Service: EC2 | Action: DeregisterTransitGatewayMulticastGroupMembers | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 deregistertransitgatewaymulticastgroupmembers --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Deregisters the specified members (network interfaces) from the transit gateway multicast group.

Service: EC2 | Action: DeregisterTransitGatewayMulticastGroupSources | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 deregistertransitgatewaymulticastgroupsources --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Deregisters the specified sources (network interfaces) from the transit gateway multicast group.

Service: EC2 | Action: DescribeAccountAttributes | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 describeaccountattributes --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Describes attributes of your Amazon Web Services account. The following are the supported account attributes:

  • default-vpc: The ID of the default VPC for your account, or none.

  • max-instances: This attribute is no longer supported. The returned value does not reflect your actual vCPU limit for running On-Demand Instances. For more information, see On-Demand Instance Limits in the Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud User Guide.

  • max-elastic-ips: The maximum number of Elastic IP addresses that you can allocate.

  • supported-platforms: This attribute is deprecated.

  • vpc-max-elastic-ips: The maximum number of Elastic IP addresses that you can allocate.

  • vpc-max-security-groups-per-interface: The maximum number of security groups that you can assign to a network interface.

The order of the elements in the response, including those within nested structures, might vary. Applications should not assume the elements appear in a particular order.

Service: EC2 | Action: DescribeAddressTransfers | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 describeaddresstransfers --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Describes an Elastic IP address transfer. For more information, see Transfer Elastic IP addresses in the Amazon VPC User Guide.

When you transfer an Elastic IP address, there is a two-step handshake between the source and transfer Amazon Web Services accounts. When the source account starts the transfer, the transfer account has seven days to accept the Elastic IP address transfer. During those seven days, the source account can view the pending transfer by using this action. After seven days, the transfer expires and ownership of the Elastic IP address returns to the source account. Accepted transfers are visible to the source account for 14 days after the transfers have been accepted.

Service: EC2 | Action: DescribeAddresses | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 describeaddresses --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Describes the specified Elastic IP addresses or all of your Elastic IP addresses.

Service: EC2 | Action: DescribeAddressesAttribute | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 describeaddressesattribute --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Describes the attributes of the specified Elastic IP addresses. For requirements, see Using reverse DNS for email applications.

Service: EC2 | Action: DescribeAggregateIdFormat | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 describeaggregateidformat --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Describes the longer ID format settings for all resource types in a specific Region. This request is useful for performing a quick audit to determine whether a specific Region is fully opted in for longer IDs (17-character IDs).

This request only returns information about resource types that support longer IDs.

The following resource types support longer IDs: bundle | conversion-task | customer-gateway | dhcp-options | elastic-ip-allocation | elastic-ip-association | export-task | flow-log | image | import-task | instance | internet-gateway | network-acl | network-acl-association | network-interface | network-interface-attachment | prefix-list | reservation | route-table | route-table-association | security-group | snapshot | subnet | subnet-cidr-block-association | volume | vpc | vpc-cidr-block-association | vpc-endpoint | vpc-peering-connection | vpn-connection | vpn-gateway.

Service: EC2 | Action: DescribeAvailabilityZones | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 describeavailabilityzones --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Describes the Availability Zones, Local Zones, and Wavelength Zones that are available to you.

For more information about Availability Zones, Local Zones, and Wavelength Zones, see Regions and zones in the Amazon EC2 User Guide.

The order of the elements in the response, including those within nested structures, might vary. Applications should not assume the elements appear in a particular order.

Service: EC2 | Action: DescribeAwsNetworkPerformanceMetricSubscriptions | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 describeawsnetworkperformancemetricsubscriptions --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Describes the current Infrastructure Performance metric subscriptions.

Service: EC2 | Action: DescribeBundleTasks | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 describebundletasks --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Describes the specified bundle tasks or all of your bundle tasks.

Completed bundle tasks are listed for only a limited time. If your bundle task is no longer in the list, you can still register an AMI from it. Just use RegisterImage with the Amazon S3 bucket name and image manifest name you provided to the bundle task.

The order of the elements in the response, including those within nested structures, might vary. Applications should not assume the elements appear in a particular order.

Service: EC2 | Action: DescribeByoipCidrs | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 describebyoipcidrs --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Describes the IP address ranges that were provisioned for use with Amazon Web Services resources through through bring your own IP addresses (BYOIP).

Service: EC2 | Action: DescribeCapacityBlockExtensionHistory | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 describecapacityblockextensionhistory --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Describes the events for the specified Capacity Block extension during the specified time.

Service: EC2 | Action: DescribeCapacityBlockExtensionOfferings | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 describecapacityblockextensionofferings --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Describes Capacity Block extension offerings available for purchase in the Amazon Web Services Region that you're currently using.

Service: EC2 | Action: DescribeCapacityBlockOfferings | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 describecapacityblockofferings --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Describes Capacity Block offerings available for purchase in the Amazon Web Services Region that you're currently using. With Capacity Blocks, you can purchase a specific GPU instance type or EC2 UltraServer for a period of time.

To search for an available Capacity Block offering, you specify a reservation duration and instance count.

Service: EC2 | Action: DescribeCapacityBlockStatus | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 describecapacityblockstatus --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Describes the availability of capacity for the specified Capacity blocks, or all of your Capacity Blocks.

Service: EC2 | Action: DescribeCapacityBlocks | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 describecapacityblocks --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Describes details about Capacity Blocks in the Amazon Web Services Region that you're currently using.

Service: EC2 | Action: DescribeCapacityManagerDataExports | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 describecapacitymanagerdataexports --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Describes one or more Capacity Manager data export configurations. Returns information about export settings, delivery status, and recent export activity.

Service: EC2 | Action: DescribeCapacityReservationBillingRequests | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 describecapacityreservationbillingrequests --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Describes a request to assign the billing of the unused capacity of a Capacity Reservation. For more information, see Billing assignment for shared Amazon EC2 Capacity Reservations.

Service: EC2 | Action: DescribeCapacityReservationFleets | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 describecapacityreservationfleets --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Describes one or more Capacity Reservation Fleets.

Service: EC2 | Action: DescribeCapacityReservationTopology | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 describecapacityreservationtopology --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Describes a tree-based hierarchy that represents the physical host placement of your pending or active Capacity Reservations within an Availability Zone or Local Zone. You can use this information to determine the relative proximity of your capacity within the Amazon Web Services network before it is launched and use this information to allocate capacity together to support your tightly coupled workloads.

Capacity Reservation topology is supported for specific instance types only. For more information, see Prerequisites for Amazon EC2 instance topology in the Amazon EC2 User Guide.

The Amazon EC2 API follows an eventual consistency model due to the distributed nature of the system supporting it. As a result, when you call the DescribeCapacityReservationTopology API command immediately after launching instances, the response might return a null value for capacityBlockId because the data might not have fully propagated across all subsystems. For more information, see Eventual consistency in the Amazon EC2 API in the Amazon EC2 Developer Guide.

For more information, see Amazon EC2 topology in the Amazon EC2 User Guide.

Service: EC2 | Action: DescribeCapacityReservations | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 describecapacityreservations --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Describes one or more of your Capacity Reservations. The results describe only the Capacity Reservations in the Amazon Web Services Region that you're currently using.

Service: EC2 | Action: DescribeCarrierGateways | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 describecarriergateways --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Describes one or more of your carrier gateways.

Service: EC2 | Action: DescribeClassicLinkInstances | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 describeclassiclinkinstances --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

This action is deprecated.

Describes your linked EC2-Classic instances. This request only returns information about EC2-Classic instances linked to a VPC through ClassicLink. You cannot use this request to return information about other instances.

Service: EC2 | Action: DescribeClientVpnAuthorizationRules | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 describeclientvpnauthorizationrules --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Describes the authorization rules for a specified Client VPN endpoint.

Service: EC2 | Action: DescribeClientVpnConnections | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 describeclientvpnconnections --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Describes active client connections and connections that have been terminated within the last 60 minutes for the specified Client VPN endpoint.

Service: EC2 | Action: DescribeClientVpnEndpoints | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 describeclientvpnendpoints --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Describes one or more Client VPN endpoints in the account.

Service: EC2 | Action: DescribeClientVpnRoutes | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 describeclientvpnroutes --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Describes the routes for the specified Client VPN endpoint.

Service: EC2 | Action: DescribeClientVpnTargetNetworks | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 describeclientvpntargetnetworks --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Describes the target networks associated with the specified Client VPN endpoint.

Service: EC2 | Action: DescribeCoipPools | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 describecoippools --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Describes the specified customer-owned address pools or all of your customer-owned address pools.

Service: EC2 | Action: DescribeConversionTasks | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 describeconversiontasks --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Describes the specified conversion tasks or all your conversion tasks. For more information, see the VM Import/Export User Guide.

For information about the import manifest referenced by this API action, see VM Import Manifest.

Service: EC2 | Action: DescribeCustomerGateways | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 describecustomergateways --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Describes one or more of your VPN customer gateways.

For more information, see Amazon Web Services Site-to-Site VPN in the Amazon Web Services Site-to-Site VPN User Guide.

Service: EC2 | Action: DescribeDeclarativePoliciesReports | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 describedeclarativepoliciesreports --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Describes the metadata of an account status report, including the status of the report.

To view the full report, download it from the Amazon S3 bucket where it was saved. Reports are accessible only when they have the complete status. Reports with other statuses (running, cancelled, or error) are not available in the S3 bucket. For more information about downloading objects from an S3 bucket, see Downloading objects in the Amazon Simple Storage Service User Guide.

For more information, see Generating the account status report for declarative policies in the Amazon Web Services Organizations User Guide.

Service: EC2 | Action: DescribeDhcpOptions | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 describedhcpoptions --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Describes your DHCP option sets. The default is to describe all your DHCP option sets. Alternatively, you can specify specific DHCP option set IDs or filter the results to include only the DHCP option sets that match specific criteria.

For more information, see DHCP option sets in the Amazon VPC User Guide.

Service: EC2 | Action: DescribeEgressOnlyInternetGateways | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 describeegressonlyinternetgateways --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Describes your egress-only internet gateways. The default is to describe all your egress-only internet gateways. Alternatively, you can specify specific egress-only internet gateway IDs or filter the results to include only the egress-only internet gateways that match specific criteria.

Service: EC2 | Action: DescribeElasticGpus | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 describeelasticgpus --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Amazon Elastic Graphics reached end of life on January 8, 2024.

Describes the Elastic Graphics accelerator associated with your instances.

Service: EC2 | Action: DescribeExportImageTasks | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 describeexportimagetasks --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Describes the specified export image tasks or all of your export image tasks.

Service: EC2 | Action: DescribeExportTasks | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 describeexporttasks --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Describes the specified export instance tasks or all of your export instance tasks.

Service: EC2 | Action: DescribeFastLaunchImages | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 describefastlaunchimages --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Describe details for Windows AMIs that are configured for Windows fast launch.

Service: EC2 | Action: DescribeFastSnapshotRestores | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 describefastsnapshotrestores --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Describes the state of fast snapshot restores for your snapshots.

Service: EC2 | Action: DescribeFleetHistory | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 describefleethistory --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Describes the events for the specified EC2 Fleet during the specified time.

EC2 Fleet events are delayed by up to 30 seconds before they can be described. This ensures that you can query by the last evaluated time and not miss a recorded event. EC2 Fleet events are available for 48 hours.

For more information, see Monitor fleet events using Amazon EventBridge in the Amazon EC2 User Guide.

Service: EC2 | Action: DescribeFleetInstances | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 describefleetinstances --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Describes the running instances for the specified EC2 Fleet.

Currently, DescribeFleetInstances does not support fleets of type instant. Instead, use DescribeFleets, specifying the instant fleet ID in the request.

For more information, see Describe your EC2 Fleet in the Amazon EC2 User Guide.

Service: EC2 | Action: DescribeFleets | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 describefleets --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Describes the specified EC2 Fleet or all of your EC2 Fleets.

If a fleet is of type instant, you must specify the fleet ID in the request, otherwise the fleet does not appear in the response.

For more information, see Describe your EC2 Fleet in the Amazon EC2 User Guide.

Service: EC2 | Action: DescribeFlowLogs | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 describeflowlogs --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Describes one or more flow logs.

To view the published flow log records, you must view the log destination. For example, the CloudWatch Logs log group, the Amazon S3 bucket, or the Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream.

Service: EC2 | Action: DescribeFpgaImageAttribute | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 describefpgaimageattribute --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Service: EC2 | Action: DescribeIdFormat | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 describeidformat --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Describes the ID format settings for your resources on a per-Region basis, for example, to view which resource types are enabled for longer IDs. This request only returns information about resource types whose ID formats can be modified; it does not return information about other resource types.

The following resource types support longer IDs: bundle | conversion-task | customer-gateway | dhcp-options | elastic-ip-allocation | elastic-ip-association | export-task | flow-log | image | import-task | instance | internet-gateway | network-acl | network-acl-association | network-interface | network-interface-attachment | prefix-list | reservation | route-table | route-table-association | security-group | snapshot | subnet | subnet-cidr-block-association | volume | vpc | vpc-cidr-block-association | vpc-endpoint | vpc-peering-connection | vpn-connection | vpn-gateway.

These settings apply to the IAM user who makes the request; they do not apply to the entire Amazon Web Services account. By default, an IAM user defaults to the same settings as the root user, unless they explicitly override the settings by running the ModifyIdFormat command. Resources created with longer IDs are visible to all IAM users, regardless of these settings and provided that they have permission to use the relevant Describe command for the resource type.

Service: EC2 | Action: DescribeIdentityIdFormat | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 describeidentityidformat --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

This request only returns information about resource types whose ID formats can be modified; it does not return information about other resource types. For more information, see Resource IDs in the Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud User Guide.

The following resource types support longer IDs: bundle | conversion-task | customer-gateway | dhcp-options | elastic-ip-allocation | elastic-ip-association | export-task | flow-log | image | import-task | instance | internet-gateway | network-acl | network-acl-association | network-interface | network-interface-attachment | prefix-list | reservation | route-table | route-table-association | security-group | snapshot | subnet | subnet-cidr-block-association | volume | vpc | vpc-cidr-block-association | vpc-endpoint | vpc-peering-connection | vpn-connection | vpn-gateway.

These settings apply to the principal specified in the request. They do not apply to the principal that makes the request.

Recently deregistered images appear in the returned results for a short interval and then return empty results. After all instances that reference a deregistered AMI are terminated, specifying the ID of the image will eventually return an error indicating that the AMI ID cannot be found.

When Allowed AMIs is set to enabled, only allowed images are returned in the results, with the imageAllowed field set to true for each image. In audit-mode, the imageAllowed field is set to true for images that meet the account's Allowed AMIs criteria, and false for images that don't meet the criteria. For more information, see Allowed AMIs.

Describes the credit option for CPU usage of the specified burstable performance instances. The credit options are standard and unlimited.

If you do not specify an instance ID, Amazon EC2 returns burstable performance instances with the unlimited credit option, as well as instances that were previously configured as T2, T3, and T3a with the unlimited credit option. For example, if you resize a T2 instance, while it is configured as unlimited, to an M4 instance, Amazon EC2 returns the M4 instance.

If you specify one or more instance IDs, Amazon EC2 returns the credit option (standard or unlimited) of those instances. If you specify an instance ID that is not valid, such as an instance that is not a burstable performance instance, an error is returned.

Recently terminated instances might appear in the returned results. This interval is usually less than one hour.

If an Availability Zone is experiencing a service disruption and you specify instance IDs in the affected zone, or do not specify any instance IDs at all, the call fails. If you specify only instance IDs in an unaffected zone, the call works normally.

For more information, see Burstable performance instances in the Amazon EC2 User Guide.

Service: EC2 | Action: DescribeInstanceEventNotificationAttributes | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 describeinstanceeventnotificationattributes --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

If you specify filters, the output includes information for only those event windows that meet the filter criteria. If you do not specify event windows IDs or filters, the output includes information for all event windows, which can affect performance. We recommend that you use pagination to ensure that the operation returns quickly and successfully.

For more information, see Define event windows for scheduled events in the Amazon EC2 User Guide.

Service: EC2 | Action: DescribeInstanceImageMetadata | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 describeinstanceimagemetadata --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Describes the AMI that was used to launch an instance, even if the AMI is deprecated, deregistered, made private (no longer public or shared with your account), or not allowed.

If you specify instance IDs, the output includes information for only the specified instances. If you specify filters, the output includes information for only those instances that meet the filter criteria. If you do not specify instance IDs or filters, the output includes information for all instances, which can affect performance.

If you specify an instance ID that is not valid, an instance that doesn't exist, or an instance that you do not own, an error (InvalidInstanceID.NotFound) is returned.

Recently terminated instances might appear in the returned results. This interval is usually less than one hour.

In the rare case where an Availability Zone is experiencing a service disruption and you specify instance IDs that are in the affected Availability Zone, or do not specify any instance IDs at all, the call fails. If you specify only instance IDs that are in an unaffected Availability Zone, the call works normally.

The order of the elements in the response, including those within nested structures, might vary. Applications should not assume the elements appear in a particular order.

Service: EC2 | Action: DescribeInstanceSqlHaStates | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 describeinstancesqlhastates --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Service: EC2 | Action: DescribeInstanceStatus | LocalStack_CLI: aws ec2 describeinstancestatus --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 | Description:

Describes the status of the specified instances or all of your instances. By default, only running instances are described, unless you specifically indicate to return the status of all instances.

Instance status includes the following components:

  • Status checks - Amazon EC2 performs status checks on running EC2 instances to identify hardware and software issues. For more information, see Status checks for your instances and Troubleshoot instances with failed status checks in the Amazon EC2 User Guide.

  • Scheduled events - Amazon EC2 can schedule events (such as reboot, stop, or terminate) for your instances related to hardware issues, software updates, or system maintenance. For more information, see Scheduled events for your instances in the Amazon EC2 User Guide.

  • Instance state - You can manage your instances from the moment you launch them through their termination. For more information, see Instance lifecycle in the Amazon EC2 User Guide.
